clue.text: Cryptic clues are mostly profane

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the word it qualifies loses its final letter
something cryptic is obscured, so the letters that follow are scrambled out of their plain order

parts.note: taken as written
the word are without its last letter

explanation.surface: A complaint that crossword clues are full of bad language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cryptic clues' reads as a single phrase about crosswords, but 'Cryptic' is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Profane in its older sense means worldly, not religious, which is exactly what secular means.

clue.text: Oscillation in power: a signal of Caesar's arrival

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the smooth repeating curve of alternating-current electricity
second meaning, punning: a sign (a gesture) of greeting as Caesar enters

explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning is a pun: say the answer as 'sign wave', the greeting a crowd gives an arriving emperor; sine is also a Latin word, fitting Caesar.
explanation.definitionFit: The voltage of alternating current rises and falls along a sine curve, so a power supply's oscillation is this smooth periodic form.

clue.text: Clown's head and arm go up

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the first letter of clown
an arm is a limb

explanation.surface: A circus clown raises his head and arm.
explanation.definitionFit: To climb is to ascend, moving upward on a slope, ladder or rope.

clue.text: Balance managed with participation of the author's bookkeeper?

parts.note: Libra, the zodiac sign, is symbolised by a pair of scales

indicators.note: participation means taking part from within, so the author's letter joins inside the word for managed

parts.note: to run a business is to manage it
the author is the setter, who refers to themself as I; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A writer's accountant balancing the books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bookkeeper' looks like an accountant, which suits 'balance', but the question mark flags a literal reading: someone who keeps books.
explanation.definitionFit: A librarian looks after a library's books, so the term is read literally as keeper of books.

clue.text: Religious ceremony is less original in the nude

indicators.note: a nude figure is stripped of its outer layer, so the word loses its outermost letters

parts.note: trite means unoriginal, so less original is more trite

explanation.surface: A complaint that a naked worship ritual is unoriginal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Less original' is a comparative adjective standing for one comparative word, and stripping removes its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A rite is a formal act of worship or ritual, such as a baptism or a marriage service.

clue.text: Our parting shot on whiskey

indicators.note: parting means splitting something apart, so another word sits in the gap that opens up

parts.note: BB is a size of small lead shot, as in a BB gun
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A farewell toast downed as a final glass of whiskey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parting shot' looks like a set phrase for a last remark or a last drink, but the shot is what gets parted, by OUR.
explanation.definitionFit: Bourbon is an American whiskey distilled mainly from corn, so it is a specific kind of the spirit.

clue.text: Where razors are wielded to prevent riotous Serb dance

parts.note: to bar is to prevent or block

indicators.note: riotous means wild and disorderly, so the letters of the next word are thrown out of order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
a hop is an informal dance

explanation.surface: Weapons drawn to stop a violent Serbian dance.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a knife fight, but the razors are a barber's and the scene is a haircut.
explanation.definitionFit: A barbershop is where barbers shave customers and cut hair, so cut-throat razors are in use there.

clue.text: Before rising, illuminated well?

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means going up the column, so the pieces are read from bottom to top

parts.note: lit means lighted up
nu is the Yiddish interjection meaning well? or so?

explanation.surface: A question about whether the well was lit up before getting up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nu' is common in American English from Yiddish; the question mark in the clue belongs to it.
explanation.definitionFit: Until and before both mark the time limit up to which something happens, as in wait until or before dawn.

clue.text: Mixture of basalt and ice in northern body of water

indicators.note: a mixture blends things together, so the letters that follow are stirred into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Volcanic rock and ice mingling in a cold northern sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The Baltic Sea is the arm of the Atlantic between Scandinavia and mainland northern Europe.

clue.text: Family member is born in Paris — what a relief!

parts.note: né is French for born
phew is the exclamation of relief

explanation.surface: Relief when a relative's baby is safely delivered in France.
explanation.definitionFit: A nephew is the son of one's brother or sister, a relative in the family.

clue.text: Reorganize retail bin in tense situation

indicators.note: to reorganize is to arrange things anew, so the letters that follow are put in a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A shop manager tidies the store's bins during a stressful moment.
explanation.definitionFit: A cliffhanger of an event is called this because it makes onlookers chew their fingernails with suspense.

clue.text: Flower's edge behind you in Guatemala

indicators.note: behind says the edge comes after the other part, so it is placed second

parts.note: tu is the familiar Spanish word for you, and Spanish is Guatemala's language
a lip is the rim or edge of a cup or crater

explanation.surface: A gardener's note about a flower bed's border in Central America.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after Flower is 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay; 'Flower's edge' wants to be one phrase but is not.
explanation.definitionFit: The tulip is a spring bulb plant grown for its cup-shaped blooms, so it is an example of the category.

clue.text: Beginning of William Shakespeare play (all but the final two parts) rewound in video device

indicators.text: all but the final two parts
indicators.note: the play's title is used except for its closing pair of letters, which are dropped
the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of William

indicators.note: rewinding a tape runs it backwards, so the shortened title is read from end to start

parts.note: Macbeth, Shakespeare's Scottish tragedy, cut short by two letters

explanation.surface: Someone watches the opening of a Shakespeare production on a VCR, rewinding it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'William Shakespeare' looks like one name, but only William's first letter is used; the play is a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A webcam is a small camera that streams video to a computer, so it counts as a piece of video equipment.

clue.text: Someone who doesn't say anything about late preparation when dinner is supposed to be ready

definitions.text: when dinner is supposed to be ready

indicators.note: about means around, so the silent performer's word surrounds the other letters

parts.note: a mime performs without speaking

indicators.note: preparation here means working something up, so the word before it is rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A sulking cook says nothing about running late with the meal.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one long scene of a silent cook, but it splits into the performer, the jumbled word and a long definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Mealtime is the scheduled hour for eating, the point at which supper should be on the table.

clue.text: Puzzle after Sunday the 15th, often: how to ride a horse while wearing a skirt

definitions.text: how to ride a horse while wearing a skirt

indicators.note: after says the puzzling word comes later, so it is placed at the end

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for Sunday
in the Roman calendar the ides fell on the 15th of March, May, July and October, the 13th otherwise
to addle is to muddle or confuse

explanation.surface: Someone tackles a newspaper puzzle on a weekend date and finds a riding tip in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Often' is there because the ides is the 15th in only four months of the year.
explanation.definitionFit: Riding sidesaddle means sitting with both legs on one side of the horse, the traditional posture for women in long skirts.

clue.text: State: "Video-game family getting last of menthol cigarettes"

parts.note: Virginia is a US state

indicators.note: getting means taking something in, so the family's name receives a letter inside it

parts.note: The Sims is a video game about a simulated household

indicators.note: the last of a word is its closing letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the closing letter of menthol

explanation.surface: A quoted statement about a gaming family taking up menthol smokes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State:' looks like an instruction to say something, but it is a noun naming the first piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Virginia Slims is an American cigarette brand marketed to women, so the name stands for a type of smokes.

clue.text: Cue to take a rest

indicators.note: to take means to receive something inside, so the cue word holds the other letter

parts.note: a cue is a prompt or reminder
taken as written

explanation.surface: A signal telling someone it is time for a break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take a rest' reads as one phrase about pausing, but 'rest' alone is the definition, in its sense of what is left over.
explanation.definitionFit: The rest of something is the part left over, which is exactly what a remainder is.

clue.text: Fantastic gain Mary and I redistributed

indicators.note: redistributed means dealt out again in a new way, so the preceding letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Two people share out a wonderful windfall between them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fantastic' looks like praise for the gain, but it is the definition in its sense of fanciful.
explanation.definitionFit: Fantastic in its original sense means existing only in fantasy, so it is a synonym for unreal or made-up.

clue.text: Windows 8 might be regarded thus: something toxic

definitions.meaning: first meaning, split into three words: as the finest operating system
second meaning: a fibrous mineral whose dust causes lung disease

explanation.surface: A dig at Microsoft's unpopular operating system, calling it poison.
explanation.walkthrough: Windows 8 is a Microsoft operating system, or OS; read the answer as three words, AS BEST OS, to get the first meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Asbestos is a fireproof mineral fibre once used in buildings, now banned because breathing it in causes cancer.

clue.text: State: "Workers mostly returning for pool hustler"

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the word for workers loses its final letter

parts.note: Minnesota is a US state

indicators.note: returning means going back the way it came, so the shortened word is read from end to start

parts.note: staff, the workers of a business, with its last letter dropped

explanation.surface: A quoted statement about staff heading back to the pool hall.
explanation.walkthrough: As in the cigarette clue, 'State:' is a noun naming the first piece, not an instruction to speak.
explanation.definitionFit: Minnesota Fats is the legendary billiards con man of the film The Hustler, a name later taken by a real player.

clue.text: Be able to buy a loud car

parts.note: taken as written
f, forte, is the musical marking for loud
a Ford is a make of car

explanation.surface: Wondering whether one has the money for a noisy automobile.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition runs into the wordplay so that 'buy a loud car' sounds like one purchase.
explanation.definitionFit: To afford something is to have enough money to pay for it.

clue.text: Liver, for example, is eaten by Rosa if chopped

indicators.note: something eaten ends up inside the eater, so one piece goes inside the other
chopped means cut up and mixed, so the letters before it are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
e.g. is the abbreviation for for example

explanation.surface: Liver is a dish Rosa would eat, provided it is cut up first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liver, for example' looks like a definition by example, but the definition is 'Liver' alone and 'for example' supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Foie gras is French for fat liver: the fattened liver of a goose or duck served as a delicacy.

clue.text: A place for putting money

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the closely mown area round a golf hole where players putt
second meaning: American slang for cash, from the colour of dollar bills

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a description of a bank or piggy bank, but 'putting' is the golf stroke, not depositing.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf the putting surface around each hole is called this, and US slang names banknotes after their colour.

clue.text: Sorceress has large group of friends

indicators.note: has means holds, so the sorceress's name contains the other letter

parts.note: Circe is the enchantress of the Odyssey who turns men into pigs
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A witch with plenty of pals.
explanation.definitionFit: A social circle is the set of people someone regularly mixes with, a ring of companions.

clue.text: Online company supporting computer peripherals' chip in Britain

indicators.note: in a down clue a supporting piece sits underneath, so the company comes second
peripherals are things at the edge, so only the outermost letters of the word are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of computer
an ISP is an internet service provider

explanation.surface: An internet firm backing a British factory that makes chips for computer accessories.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Computer peripherals' means keyboards and mice in the surface, but here it means the edges of the word computer. An American potato chip is a crisp in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: British English calls a thin fried potato slice sold in bags a crisp, where Americans say chip.

clue.text: Game with remote ring?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a popular Xbox video game series
second meaning: a circle of light floating apart from a saint's head

explanation.surface: A video game played with a ring-shaped controller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Remote' suggests a games controller, but it means apart: the ring hovers above the head without touching it, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Halo is the title of Microsoft's science-fiction shooter, and also the glowing circle painted above saints.

clue.text: Look back and check out a song that used to be popular

definitions.text: a song that used to be popular

indicators.note: back means going the other way, so the word for look is read from end to start

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look, as in lo and behold
to check out is slang for to die

explanation.surface: Someone looks back nostalgically and listens to a former hit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Check out' sounds like listening to a song, but it is slang for dying.
explanation.definitionFit: An oldie is a hit record from years ago, still played for nostalgia.

clue.text: Rug is described by darn playwright

indicators.note: to describe a figure is to draw a line around it, so one word encloses the others

parts.note: darn and drat are both mild curses
taken as written
a mat is a small rug

explanation.surface: A stage writer curses at the rug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Darn' suggests mending the rug, but it is the exclamation; 'described' is used in its geometry sense of drawing round.
explanation.definitionFit: A dramatist writes plays for the stage, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Comedian seen in unrated flop

indicators.note: a flop is a failure that falls apart, so the preceding word is broken up and rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A comic appears in an unclassified film that bombed.
explanation.definitionFit: Jimmy Durante was an American entertainer famous for his big nose and gravelly singing, a classic vaudeville and film funnyman.

clue.text: Mountain with rotten plums, yo!

indicators.note: rotten fruit has gone soft and fallen apart, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A hiker shouts about a peak covered in spoilt fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yo' looks like a throwaway exclamation for the surface, but its letters are needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Olympus is the highest peak in Greece, home of the gods in Greek myth.
